title: A cast argument inside a loop is hoisted into a saved register.
symptom: one more saved register than retail, set to a stack array's address (`addiu s6,sp,N`) before a loop and copied into `a0` for a call inside it, and a frame 16 bytes larger; retail recomputes `addiu a0,sp,N` at the call like every other use of the array.
cause: `f((int)path)` against a callee declared with an `int` parameter makes the argument a conversion node; the optimizer moves that loop-invariant expression out of the loop, while a bare array address is left in place.
spelling: declare the callee with its real pointer parameter and pass `path`.

title: A release written through the field rereads it.
symptom: A macro that names `file->_media` at each use reloads the field after the count store; retail's single read comes from the form that takes one local copy (`RELEASE_REF`).

title: A field test through a pointer parameter shares the field's address across a store.
symptom: after `meta->_validity |= 8`, the next tests read the field through a computed address (`addiu v1,s2,36` ... `lw v1,0(v1)`) where retail reloads `lw v1,36(s2)`.
cause: an inline test taking `const igMetaObject *` gives the common-subexpression pass the address `meta + 36` to share between the update and the test.
spelling: the test takes the object by reference, `hasValidity(const igMetaObject &meta, int bit)`.

title: Two loads merge only when their types agree, `const` included.
symptom: a store reloads a pointer field the walk already loaded (`_data` loaded twice).
cause: `IRO_CommonSubs` compares node types exactly. A getter taking `const List *` reads `_data` as a pointer to `const`, a setter taking `List *` as a plain pointer: two expressions.
spelling: getter and setter take the same pointer type. Pointer-typed loads `T *` and `T *const` merge, as do two different pointer types; `int`/`const int`, `int`/`unsigned` and `int`/pointer do not.

title: A read through a `const` object is marked, and loop rotation keeps the mark.
symptom: a `for` loop's body reloads a field its own condition just loaded, while a neighbouring loop on a plain field shares the load.
cause: every pointer-valued IR node carries the qualifier of its target; a field read through a `const` object (`this` of a `const` member, a `const T &`) has its address node marked. `IRO_RotateLoop` copies the condition in front of the loop with the mark; `IRO_MoveInvariantsInAddressExpr` rebuilds the address inside the loop without it. The node comparison requires equal flags, so the guard and the body are different expressions, and the body is a merge of two edges on which the value is not available. It needs the loop and something in it (a call, a store) that stops the read being hoisted.
spelling: a `const` accessor taking the owner by reference, the way a `const` member function takes `this`: `static inline Util *utilOf(const Owner &o) { return (Util *)o._util; }`, used in the condition and the body alike.

title: A `const` reference is not a pointer to `const`.
symptom: with a `const T *` accessor or cast the field's address is computed before the loop (`addiu a0,s0,52`) and loaded inside it; retail has no such instruction.
cause: the qualification conversion `T *` to `const T *` is an IR node of its own, so `(const T *)p + 52` is a loop-invariant expression and is hoisted. Binding a reference, or `this` of a member function, makes no conversion node.
spelling: take the object by `const T &`, or use a `const` member function.

title: A cast that only retypes a read makes a different tree.
symptom: `*(int *)&o->f` or a smart-pointer view of an `int` field puts a conversion node between the address and the load, so that read never merges with a plain one. That is why one such read in exactly one of two places "works": it is a symptom of the two reads needing to differ, not the source. Look for the real reason the original's reads differ (the `const` mark above, an accessor).
unit_text: `src/game/beNDMWLoadCtrl2.cpp`; one such read is still open in `src/game/beNDMWShopCtrl00.cpp`.

title: Inline `const` accessors through a smart-pointer field keep a byte offset beside the index.
symptom: a search loop loads the list once, reloads the count every pass, hoists `_data` and keeps a byte offset in a register beside the index; plain field reads give a hoisted count and a walking pointer.
cause: each inlined accessor leaves the pointer `operator->() const` returned in a temporary assigned where the call stands, behind a conversion. The body's temporary is assigned inside the loop, so `_data` is not an invariant base and `IRO_DoStrengthReduction` makes `i * 4` an offset stepped beside `i` instead of a walking pointer. The count read through `getCount() const` is `const int`; the guard's copy and the bottom test's are not merged, so it loads every pass. The code generator then hoists the `_data` load, because it hoists out of a loop's first block only. Registers follow creation order: index, row, offset, list, so the list colours first.
spelling: the Alchemy idiom on the object-reference field held as a smart pointer: `for (int i = 0; i < ((ListRef &)self->_list)->getCount(); i++) { Row *row = ((ListRef &)self->_list)->get(i); }` with `getCount() const` and `get(int) const` on the list class. It reproduces the GameCube and Xbox loops as well, and needs no declaration order.

title: A `const` parameter or local is bound before the expression.
symptom: a loaded value is the second operand of a multiply, or a load comes earlier than the plain spelling puts it.
cause: b52 binds a `const` local, or the `const` parameter of an inlined function, to its argument before the body runs; a plain one is folded back into the expression.
spelling: `static inline long long FramesToTime(const float frames)`. The older form `x = p->v; x = x;` gives the same code and has no reason.

title: An inlined getter's result is a value of its own.
symptom: `owned->_kazu = DiskCount(owned) + self->_kazu` gives retail's `addu` operand order where every plain spelling flips it; a getter for the selected row does the same for an index sum.

title: A conversion on an operand makes it evaluate first.
symptom: three components of a local vector each times one float constant; retail has the first component in `$f3` and the constant in `$f2`, every plain spelling has them exchanged.
cause: the optimizer puts the constant on the left of each product and the code generator makes the constant's temporary first, so it has the lowest allocator id and colours last (constant 32, x 33, traced). A component whose load carries two conversion nodes is evaluated before the constant (x 32, constant 33): a value conversion over the load, which a `const float` copied by value leaves behind when the copy is propagated into the product, and a pointer conversion under it, between the local's address and the load. Either one alone changes nothing: `const` and by value but indexed as `(&x)[i]` or `v[i]`, or the pointer cast with a reference return or without `const`, all give the exchanged registers.
spelling: `static inline float fadeLimit(const Work *w) { return w->_fadeLimit; }`. / the vector's `const` element accessor returning by value, `float operator[](int i) const { return ((const float *)this)[i]; }`, and the call written out: `MakeEuler(matrix, 0.017453292f * rotation[0], 0.017453292f * rotation[1], 0.017453292f * rotation[2])`. An inline that copies only `x` into a local from a `const Vec3 &` bound to a `float[3]` gave the same bytes by making the same two nodes on one component; one is enough because the constant is shared.
notes: A float compare whose limit operand carries any conversion (a `const` getter's implicit `T *` to `const T *`) loads that operand later, into the later FP register.

title: A `const` reference getter reloads.
symptom: `const int &getCount() const { return _count; }` loads through the returned reference, so a later `_count + 1` reads memory again, and the value lands in the caller's declared variable with its early id. It replaced a `volatile` count. The getter is `igTDataList<T>::getCount` in `include/dw4/igTDataList.h`.

title: A constant compared, then copied in the taken branch, is read twice.
symptom: after a call, `lw a1,<object>; lw a0,0(v1); lw v1,<object>; bne a0,v1`, and the taken path stores `a1`: one object loaded twice in a row, the first load used only after the branch.
cause: the comparison and the copy both read the member through a `const T &` parameter (`operator==`, the copy constructor), as a `const int`. `IRO_CommonSubs` shares the two reads in a temporary assigned in front of the comparison. The next round's `IRO_ExpressionPropagation` puts the temporary's expression, a plain read of a named object, back into the uses in the temporary's own block. That is the comparison; the copy is in the next block and keeps the temporary. The read put back has lost the `const` mark and the temporary's own read keeps it, so the two are different expressions from then on and each is loaded. `const` on the object plays no part, since the mark comes from the parameters. Four spellings lose the second read: a `mutable` member (or `T &` parameters) makes every read a plain `int`, and one load then serves both; a read through a cast (`*(T *)&object`) is not put back; a helper that reads the value into an `int` before the comparison has both uses in one block, where they are put back and shared again (it gave two reads on a writable object only because `int` and `const int` reads never merge); and a store ahead of the copy in the branch drops the temporary, leaving one read before the branch and one after.
spelling: `if (call() == g_resultFailure) return g_resultFailure;`, or `result = g_resultFailure;` as the branch's first statement, with the object declared as the result class (`igResult`).

title: A sorted search copies its key through a pointer.
symptom: before a binary search the key is stored to one stack slot, loaded, stored to a second slot, and the second slot is loaded again for the final equality test after the loop.
cause: the caller's key is a local whose address is passed, and the search copies `*item` into a local of its own and reads that copy through a pointer, so both locals live in memory.
spelling: `T key = light; index = list->sortedFind(&key);` with `igTDataList<T>::sortedFind(const T *item)`, whose body starts `value = *item; p = &value; key = *p;`. The order of its locals was found by a declaration-order search and is marked as such.

title: An index passed on stays an `addiu`.
symptom: `addiu v1,v0,-1; sll; addu; lw 0(v0)` for the top of a stack, where `_data[_count - 1]` written in place folds the `- 1` into the load as `lw -4(v0)`. The index as an inline accessor's argument (`stack->get(stack->_count - 1)` with `T get(int index) const`) or as a named local (`int last = count - 1;`) keeps the subtraction.

title: In a loop built for size, an indexed read is loaded on every pass.
symptom: a scan loop reloads one table word each pass, through an address computed once before the loop, though nothing in the loop stores or calls and the word was already loaded for a test in front of the loop. A pointer local read as `*w` shares the load and is 20 bytes short; a cast on the pointer (`*(unsigned *)w`) keeps the read and is not the source.
cause: written as `table[word]`, the read has an invariant address expression. `IRO_MoveInvariantExpressions` moves that address to a temporary in front of the loop and leaves the load of it inside: the unit builds `-O4,s`, which keeps the loop's test at the bottom behind a jump, so the read is not in the loop's first block. `IRO_CommonSubs` then makes the temporary a copy of the address the earlier read computed (one `addu`, one register), but a load through the temporary is not the expression loaded before the loop, so it stays. A pointer local leaves no address to move: `*w` in the loop is the expression read before it and takes its value. Under `-O4,p` the loop is rotated and the same source shares the load.
spelling: index the table at every read (`if (mask & table[word])`), with no pointer or value local. The same source compiled by CodeWarrior for GameCube 2.6 with `-O4,s` gives the GameCube build's function word for word, which also settled the statement order, a `>= 1` comparison and the parameter's pointer type. The Xbox build shares the load, so the source has no `volatile`.

title: In a loop built for size the count is hoisted and `_data` is not: the list idiom again.
symptom: a list walk loads the list and its count once in front of the loop and `_data` on every pass (`lw a2,20(a0); lw v1,8(a2)` before, `lw v0,16(a2)` inside), with the count in `v1` and the scaled index in `a0`. A list local, plain field reads, a count local and `count()`/`get()` on a cast pointer all give the same instructions with the count and the scaled index exchanged, four bytes longer because the delay slot of the loop's branch stays empty.
cause: under `-O4,s` the loop is entered at its test, so the test is the loop's first block and the code generator hoists the loads the test holds, the list and the count; the body's `_data` load stays. That needs the optimizer to have left the count in the test: the pointer `operator->() const` returns is a temporary assigned where the call stands, which keeps the read from being moved as an invariant (an assignment written in the condition does the same). A count the optimizer hoists takes the register after the scaled index; the allocator's numbering of the two was not traced.
spelling: `for (int i = 0; i < ((ListRef &)self->_objects)->count(); i++) { T *o = ((ListRef &)self->_objects)->get(i); }`. An assignment inside the condition (`while (i < (list = self->_objects)->_count)`) and the pair count kept in the function's first parameter were stand-ins for it, and so were extra arguments passed to a variadic callee to hold the index and the object in `t0` and `t1`: with the idiom the callees take their real three and four arguments.

title: Both list walks in one function.
symptom: A function that first searches one list and then walks another has the first count in the register after the scaled index and the second count in the register before it. The search is an inline helper with `list->_count` in its condition (the optimizer hoists that count); the walk is the smart-pointer idiom above. The list handed on after the loop goes through the holder's `get()`, a `const` read that shares the load hoisted for the walk (`move a0,t2`; the plain field read loads again). A named local for the searched list, which the walk's inner loop reads again, gave that node so many neighbours that it was coloured first and took the lowest register; with the field read in place every local is declared where it is first set and no declaration order is left to choose.

title: A second read of a field through a `const` getter is a second load.
symptom: `lw s1,60(s2); jal TerminateThread; lw a0,60(s2)`: the id saved for later and the id passed to the call are loaded separately with nothing between them. The saved copy is a plain read (`int id = self->_threadID;`), the argument goes through the class's `const` getter, a `const int` read. The getter on the saved copy instead gives the two loads too but numbers the copy after the call's result, and their saved registers are exchanged.

title: Calling a member of a smart-pointer local changes its destructor's release.
symptom: a function holds a returned smart pointer in a stack slot, reads it once into a register for its tests, reads it again for a call's argument, and its destructor's release, at the early return and at the end, reads the slot once. With every read spelled `.p` each release reads the slot again after storing the count (8 bytes more); with every read spelled `get()` the early return loads the slot twice (4 bytes more).
cause: the inliner folds the release's parameter back into `found.p`, read wherever the parameter is used, as long as nothing takes the local's address. A member call does (`this`), and the parameter is then bound to a temporary once. The destructor's read is unmarked; a read through a `const` accessor is marked and is not shared with it. Retail's first read is shared with the early return's release, so it is unmarked, and the argument's read comes from a member call. With non-`const` accessors `entry = found.get()` and `call(found.get())` give retail's bytes; the shared class's accessors are `const` (184 uses outside this unit), so the first read is the member itself.
spelling: `Entry *entry = (Entry *)found.p; ... remaining = unload((Handle *)found.get());`.

title: A temporary smart pointer's release reloads the pointer.
symptom: a freshly created object is assigned to a field, then released with the slot read twice: `lw v1,104(sp); beqz v1; lw v0,4(v1); addiu v0,v0,-1; sw v0,4(v1); lw a0,104(sp); lw v0,4(a0); dsll32 ...`. The out-of-line destructor of the same template (0x130140, and five copies in this unit) reads the member once, so the reload looked like a second holder class with a re-reading destructor.
cause: the holder is a temporary: built in an argument bound to a `const igSmartPointer<T> &` parameter of an inline, or returned by value and used in place. Its destructor runs at the end of the full expression with the release's parameter folded back into the temporary's member, as in the entry above. A named local passed to the same inline has its address taken and is released from one read (0x2e3a60: 580 bytes against retail's 588). The compiler pass was not traced.
spelling: `assignReference(self->_file, igSmartPointer<igFileView>(create(pool)));` and `found = openPath(self, folder.p->vfunc_23(name));`, written in the function itself. The same call inside a second inline helper's `return` reads once (0x305d30: 1152 against 1160).

title: A returned pointer taken through the holder's conversion keeps its own copy for the release.
symptom: `lw s0,140(sp); move a0,s0; beqz a0; move v0,s0`, with the count updated through `a0`: `return holder;` (`operator T *`) or `return holder.get();`. `return holder.p;` shares the read with the destructor and updates the count through `s0` (856 bytes against 868).

title: A base pointer the walk keeps is a field read, not the cursor.
symptom: `end = list->data + list->count` after `s = list->data` shares one load of `data` with the cursor's start and with the `s - list->data` the function returns, and that shared value keeps its own register; `end = s + list->count` makes the cursor the base and exchanges the base's register with the compared word's. The order of the two statements does not matter.

title: One address spelled two ways is computed twice.
symptom: A stack buffer's member address used by two calls in a loop (`entry.name` for a format and for an `igStringRef`) is common-subexpression-eliminated into a saved register; retail builds it at each use (`addiu a3,sp,208` and later `addiu s3,sp,208`). Spelling one use as pointer arithmetic (`(char *)(&entry.stat + 1)`, the byte after the stat) and the other as the member keeps them apart; casts or `&entry.name[0]` on the same member are folded together.

title: A cast between a base and a field leaves an address to move, and reads that do not merge.
symptom: a function with loops has one more 16-byte stack slot than retail and loads a byte through a spilled pointer (`lw v0,176(sp); lbu v0,0(v0)`) where retail reads it off the base (`lbu v1,75(s2)`); and a validity check loads one header byte three times where retail loads it once and masks it (`andi v0,v0,0xff`).
cause: the state record declared its bins as raw bytes and its top chunk as `char *`, so each use went through a cast to the chunk type. The cast is a node between the base and the field offset: inside a loop the cast address is an invariant expression, moved to a temporary in front of the loop, and the temporary is spilled. A cast pointer passed to three inline accessors gives three reads that are not shared; the member read in its own type is one expression, shared in a byte temporary.
spelling: type the members: the top as a pointer to the chunk header, a bin as a struct whose first member is the header, and `&state->bins[i].header` for a bin. The other functions of the allocator matched with either typing; only the ones with loops tell them apart.

title: A local that only ever holds zero is added as the zero register.
symptom: `addu v0,v0,zero` after a call, in front of the add that sums the result (objdump prints it as `move v0,v0`; the compiler's own moves are `daddu`). No type of the sum or of the callee gives it.
cause: the source adds a non-`const` local whose value is 0. `IRO_CopyAndConstantPropagation` replaces the local with 0 after the front end's folding has run, and `IRO_ConstantFolding` only moves the constant to the right: it does not remove `x + 0`. A literal `+ 0` and a `const int` are folded by the front end.
spelling: `int padding = 0;` and `size += field->ioSize(object) + padding;`. Where the local is declared and which side of the sum it stands on make no difference. What the zero stood for in the original is not known; the name is a guess.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2d5960). The graphics library has the same instruction after a load (0x17f1bc).

title: An expression goes back into its use only when the variable has one use in its block and none in another.
symptom: Read from the compiler (`IRO_ExpressionPropagation`, 0x5263b0): for each assignment `v = expression` it counts the uses of `v` in the same flow node; a constant or a plain copy is always propagated, any other expression only when that count is 1 and no other flow node reads `v`. Flow nodes are not merged again once the pass loop has started. `v += constant` is merged into the later uses by `IRO_PropagateSelfAssignments`; `v += <a load>` stays as it is, even when `v` holds a known constant. What this means for registers: the optimizer's variables (declared locals, an inline's parameters and locals, the optimizer's temporaries, in the order they are made) take their allocator ids before every expression temporary of the code generator, so a value that stays a variable is coloured after the expression temporaries around it, and a value that is put back into its use is coloured before the variables.

title: The list reserve in front of an append: the capacity is shared by the code generator, not the optimizer.
symptom: five functions double a list's capacity when `count + n` no longer fits (`lw count; lw capacity; add; slt at,capacity,sum; beqz at; sll a1,capacity,1; lw count; slt; bnez; jal`), with the sum in the count's register `v1` and the capacity in `v0`. A helper or plain field reads give the same instructions with `v0`/`v1` exchanged.
cause: with plain reads `IRO_CommonSubs` shares the capacity between the test and the doubling in a temporary of its own, which is numbered before the code generator's temporaries for the count and the sum, so the sum colours first and takes `v0`. In retail the optimizer shares nothing: each read goes through its own `operator->() const` temporary, the two capacity reads are still different expressions when `IRO_CommonSubs` runs, and the final IR has `count + n > capacity` as one expression in the first block and `capacity * 2` in the next. The code generator then evaluates count, sum, capacity in that order and reuses the capacity's load in the following block itself, so the capacity has the last number and colours first. The count is read again for the setter's own test because that read is not through the `const` accessor. What keeps a variable out of its use was read from `IRO_ExpressionPropagation` on the way: an assignment whose value is used, a right side holding a call, an assignment or a `volatile`, a second use in the block, a use in another block, or a store or call between the assignment and the use.
spelling: the list idiom on the object-reference field, with `const` accessors for both members and the list's capacity setter: `if (((ListRef &)self->_list)->count() + n > ((ListRef &)self->_list)->capacity()) setCapacity(((ListRef &)self->_list).get(), ((ListRef &)self->_list)->capacity() * 2);` with `setCapacity(list, capacity) { if (capacity >= list->_count) List_Reserve(list, capacity, sizeof(T)); }`. A count kept for later is read through the same accessor first (`offset = ((ListRef &)…)->count();` then `length + offset > …capacity()`): the two functions that held the sum with an assignment inside a helper's argument (0x2d3be0, 0x30d230) give retail's bytes with it too.

title: Trivial inline members are calls inside an expanded constructor or helper.
symptom: a constructor or helper is expanded into its caller, yet every inline it uses is a `jal`, down to empty constructors (`jr ra; move v0,a0`) and two-store setters; the same members cost nothing elsewhere.
cause: the unit builds with `-inline bottomup`. Bottom-up inlining expands an inline function's callees first, and when that would take the function past `inline_max_size` (256) it keeps all of them as calls and still expands the function itself. Top-down inlining expands everything, and `-inline level=1` gives the same calls but also in every small helper of the unit.
spelling: the members inline in their one shared header and the unit's row on `-inline level=8,bottomup`. An out-of-line declaration in a private copy of the class gives the same bytes and is not the source. The copies the linker dropped are `duplicates` of the unit, so the unit holding retail's copy is bottom-up too. The reverse case: a hand-made helper that calls inline helpers and is fully expanded in retail was not a function holding inline calls; write the statements in place.
unit_text: `src/engine/igViewerGuiFactory.cpp`; the reverse case in `src/engine/gfx/igVisualContextCapabilityManager_tail.inc`. The measurements are in [build profiles](build-profiles.md).

title: A scoped object with a constructor and a destructor keeps its member in memory.
symptom: a pointer the function already holds in a saved register is stored to the stack and loaded back before each of two calls (`sw s1,172(sp); lw a1,172(sp)`), and nothing else uses the slot.
cause: a local of a class with a destructor is not scalarized; its inline constructor and destructor read the member through the object.
spelling: the original's scoped helper: a struct holding the pointer whose constructor and destructor make the call, declared in the guarded block. Its out-of-line destructor copy is a `stripped` row.

title: A check that cannot fail still shares its loads.
symptom: a field is loaded ahead of a guard and first used after it, with no reload, while every later use reloads it.
cause: the source tests the field in a check whose condition is constant, ahead of the guard. Common subexpression elimination gives the dead check and the live one a shared temporary before the dead one is removed, and the temporary's load stays where the dead check stood. Two dead checks before the guard number the temporary differently from one.
spelling: keep the original's constant checks, in place.

title: An inlined `void` helper's early `return` jumps to the caller's single return.
symptom: the fall-through branches to the function's one `return *this`, the other case goes straight to a loop test, and an early `return *this` written in place costs a second return sequence.
spelling: the iterator's `next()` step as an inline with `if (node != 0) return;`, called from `operator++`.

title: A statement macro stops a tail call under GCC 2.96.
symptom: `j` where retail keeps `jal` and the frame: under 2.96 a loop statement around or after the call prevents the sibling call, and `do { ... } while (0)` is one.
spelling: `#define LOCK() do { lock(); } while (0)`.

title: A statement macro also pins store order under GCC 2.96.
symptom: Independent stores stay in source order where the first scheduling pass would move the argument's store first: a loop statement's notes are a scheduling barrier, and an empty `do { } while (0)` at function entry is enough. An `if (0)` or an empty block is not.

title: An `else if` chain with an empty first arm.
symptom: `beq x,1` past the arm then `bne x,2`: MWCC keeps the empty arm's compare.

title: A switch with an explicit empty case.
symptom: A compare chain `beq 2; beq 1; beqz end; b end` is a switch with `case 0: break;` and the cases in that order; without `case 0` the function is 8 bytes short, with `case 0: return;` 8 long.

title: A constant on the left keeps `slt`.
symptom: `if (capacity >= list->_count)` with `capacity` 0 gives `slt zero,count` and `bnez`, where `count <= 0` folds to `blez`; a `bool` local compared `== false` keeps the materialised test.

title: A conditional expression keeps both arms; an `if`/`else` that assigns a variable to itself loses one.
symptom: `beqz flag; b; move a0,v0` around a second call whose result is also moved to `a0` is `pool = g_useOwnerAllocator ? pool : Memory_GetAllocatorBySelector(...)`. Written as `if (flag) pool = pool; else pool = ...;` the self-assignment is deleted and the function is 8 bytes short; `pool = (int)pool;` kept it only because the cast hides the self-assignment.

title: A bare truth test that opens a loop condition is materialised.
symptom: `sltu v1,zero,a0; xori v1,v1,0x1; bnez` for the first operand of `while (*a && *b && *a == *b)`, and a plain `beqz` for the second: the strcmp shape written plainly. `*a != 0` there folds to `beqz`, and a `(bool)` cast is not needed. The remaining count of a bounded scan does the same in `while (remaining && *p)`, with the cursor declared before the count.

title: A `goto` into the tail keeps a loop's constants inside it.
symptom: a chunk walk loads `li v1,1` and `li v1,-4` on every pass in retail, and the `if (cur != top) { while … }` spelling hoists both in front of the loop (same length, other registers).
cause: with the loop inside an `if` the optimizer has a place for a pre-header. Written flat, with the skip as a jump over the loop to a label in the function's last block, it hoists nothing.
spelling: `if (cur == top) goto reset; while (walk < end) { … } … if (inUse == 0) { remove(); reset: …; return success; } return failure;`. The label sits inside the final `if`, which also puts the failure return last, as in retail.

title: A value computed on every pass is hoisted with a guard; one under `||` is not.
symptom: retail tests `0 < count` once (`sltu at,zero,n; beqz at`), loads `pool->_poolIndex >> 1 < 32` in that guarded block (placed at the end of the function) and still jumps to the loop test. With `if (size >= 0x80000 || (unsigned)pool->_poolIndex >> 1 >= 32)` in the body the load stays in the loop and there is no guard.
cause: the second operand of `||` does not run on every pass, so it is not invariant code to move. As an inline's argument (or a body local) the shift runs unconditionally; the optimizer moves it, and because it is a load it guards the moved block with the loop test. The widened `unsigned short` count is moved the same way, which is why no count local may be declared: `i < count` on the parameter.

title: An early return of a variable holding zero gets its own return block.
symptom: `list = 0; if (inProgress) return list;` is propagated to `return 0` and compiled as `b; move v0,zero` in the middle of the function; retail's test branches straight to the shared `move v0,s1` in front of the epilogue, which is the body enclosed in `if (!inProgress) { ... }` with one `return list;` after it.

title: An unsigned `-4` is one value for the header lookup and the rounding mask.
symptom: `li s0,-4` in each of three arms that find a block's header (`addiu s1,s4,-4` beside it uses the immediate), and the rounding after the join is `and a0,v0,s0`; in a sibling the value is stored to a stack slot in each arm. With `p - 4` the mask is loaded where it is used.
cause: `p - sizeof(int)` subtracts an unsigned constant, which the optimizer keeps as the same typed value as the `~3` of `(size + 3) & ~3` on an unsigned size. Where every path to the rounding has looked a header up, common subexpression elimination gives the value one temporary, assigned in each arm; three assignments reach the join, so it is not propagated back as a constant. On the free path one arm skips the lookup and nothing is shared.
spelling: the header lookup subtracts `sizeof(int)`.

title: An `unsigned short` held in a local is masked again where it is widened.
symptom: `lhu v0,0(s1); beqz v0,L; nop; andi v0,v0,0xffff; subu s1,s1,v0` is `unsigned short offset = record->offset; if (offset) first = (GangRecord *)((char *)record - offset);`. Tested as `offset != 0`, or read from the field both times, the `andi` is gone. A truth test of an `unsigned short` parameter reads the register unmasked (`beqz s2`), a comparison masks it first (`andi v0,s2,0xffff; beqz v0`).

title: Byte-returning callees make `& 0xFF` natural.
symptom: b52 emits `andi v,v0,0xff` after a call only when the result of a byte-returning function is compared (`f() == 0`, `== 1`), never for a truth test (`if (f())`). Each retail `andi 0xff` before a branch is the compare of a function declared `unsigned char` or `bool`; an explicit mask is not the source, and an `int` declaration of a byte function drops it.

title: `const bool &` and `const int &` literal temporaries become data.
symptom: A literal passed by `const &` to an inline becomes an anonymous `@N` object per call: a one-byte `.sdata` constant for a `bool`, a `.rodata` word for an `int`. Retail data that looks like a named flag table can be these.

title: An inlined `operator+=` gives a frameless function an exception record.
symptom: Retail keeps an exception record for a leaf with no frame. `*vertex += shift;` through an inline `igVec3f &operator+=(const igVec3f &o) { x += o.x; y += o.y; z += o.z; return *this; }` keeps it and explains the odd register use; `x = x + o.x` in the operator, a by-value parameter or plain float adds do not. The internal rule is not known.

title: A local whose address goes to a pointer parameter gets a stack slot.
symptom: A value stored to the stack and loaded back for a store, with no `volatile`: `pushed = item; ... set(count, &pushed);` with `void set(int i, T *const *v) { _data[i] = *v; }`. A reference parameter, a by-value parameter with an internal `&value`, or a one-field struct are scalarised and lose the slot. The setter is `igTDataList<T>::set` in `include/dw4/igTDataList.h`.

title: A negated flag passed to a `bool` parameter normalises first.
symptom: `sltu v0,zero,v0; xori a1,v0,0x1` before a call is `!attr->_enabled` passed to a virtual taking `bool`; with an `int` parameter `!x` compiles to a different sequence, and only the explicit `(x != 0) ^ 1` reproduces it.

title: Open: two `xori 1` in a row.
symptom: Retail tests the interrupt-enable bit as `andi 1; sltu; xori 1; xori 1; andi 0xff` before a branch, and no spelling found keeps both `xori`s. What the compiler does with `!`: The optimizer keeps `!!x` (`ELOGNOT(ELOGNOT(x))`); the front end folds it only when `x` is already a `bool`. A lowering pass before code generation wraps every `!` operand that is not a comparison, `!`, `&&` or `||` in `x != 0` (that is the `sltu`). The code generator emits each `!` as exactly one `xori dst,src,1`; a conversion of a `!` result to a wider or other byte type adds `andi 0xff`, and one of a comparison adds nothing. The pairs disappear in a PCode peephole on `xori`, run once per basic block after the block's def-use links are built. It turns `xori c,b,1` into a copy of `a` when the instruction defining `b` is `xori b,a,1` in the same block, the immediates are equal, and `a` is not redefined in between nor by the second `xori`. When the definition of `b` is a copy, the copy is propagated first and the handler runs again. The `andi 0xff` of an `sltu` result also goes. Retail's pair therefore had something between the two at that point: a copy that could not be propagated (its source redefined before the second `!`), a block boundary removed later by the block pass, or the second `xori` writing the first one's source register. About 50,000 generated spellings (inline nesting to three levels, `bool`/`char`/`int` locals and returns, `^ 1`, `== 0`, ternaries, `if`/`else` assignments, compound `^=`, casts between the negations, reused and twice-used locals) all fold the pair, put an `andi 0xff` or an `sltu` between the two, or keep a single `xori`.

title: A class-scope placement `delete` makes the constructor-throws cleanup.
symptom: `new (pool) T` with a matching `operator delete(void *, Pool *)` in the class gives the landing pad and exception table retail has around the constructor call.

title: An aggregate initializer copy gives a struct's real size.
symptom: A local initialised from a `.data` template is copied whole (`lq`/`sq` loop), and the template's size in retail is the struct's size; that settled a 48-byte Sony struct a 36-byte header had cut short.

title: An empty smart-pointer result built through the retaining constructor keeps its reference test.
symptom: an early-return path stores 0 into the returned holder and loads it straight back for a reference-count test (`sw zero,0(s1); lw a0,0(s1); beqz a0`) that can never pass.
cause: a by-value class result lives in the caller's memory behind the hidden result pointer. The retaining constructor's `retain()` reads the member it just stored through that pointer, and the read is not folded to the constant.
spelling: `return igSmartPointer<igObject>(0, kRetainReference);`. The default constructor leaves the test out (the function is 40 bytes short). For the holder that is returned on the other path, the adopting constructor `list(create(...))` is the source; a default-constructed `list` assigned afterwards keeps a dead `sw zero` in a delay slot.

title: Soft-float `double` arithmetic is written as `double`.
symptom: A run of `litodp`, `dpmul`, `dpdiv`, `dpadd`, `__floatdidf`, `__fixdfdi`, `__divdi3` and `__moddi3` calls with the same integer constant loaded before several of them is plain arithmetic on a `double` and a `long long`: the unit has no hardware doubles, so b52 calls a helper for every operation, and it converts an integer constant to `double` at run time (`litodp(1000000000)`) instead of folding it. `(long long)(1000000000 * seconds)` and `(double)(ns / 1000000000) + (double)(ns % 1000000000) / 1000000000` give the calls in retail's order, with the right operand of the sum evaluated first. Helper calls written out by hand with `int` arguments are not the source.

title: The stack object of a vtable getter is an instance of the class.
symptom: The frame is the 16-byte save area plus the class's registered instance size, rounded up to 16, so a 20-byte class gives the 48-byte frame; a local padded by hand to the slot's apparent 32 bytes is not needed.

title: The frame holds address-taken locals in declaration order, and a class local is built where it is declared.
symptom: Locals whose address is passed (out-parameters of a reader) lie from the top of the frame downwards in the order they are declared, one-byte ones packed, whatever order they are used in, so the slots give the original declaration block. A local of a class with a constructor is initialised at its declaration and destroyed in reverse order at the end: the position of its zero store among the surrounding statements shows where the block stands (after the first assignments, not at the top of the function), and the order of the releases at the end gives the construction order. Six interned strings released by hand in an odd order were six string holders declared in two groups around the integers.

title: A result copied from a base-class call is assigned, not initialised.
symptom: `jal base; lw s0,108(sp)` right after the call, the result kept in a saved register to the end: `igResult result; result = Base::configure(info);` leaves the returned temporary in its slot and copies it. `igResult result = base(...)` builds the call's value in the local's own slot, which stays in memory and is loaded at the return (4 bytes less); returning the call itself becomes a jump. The callee is declared with its `igResult` return, not an output pointer and an `int`.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2f0880 and the five pools' configure functions).

title: Status results that take their slots in call order come from callees that return `igResult`.
symptom: The frame holds one 4-byte slot per call, assigned downwards in the order of the calls (a semaphore `wait`, the RPC call, the `signal`s on each return path), and a test of a result reloads it through its address (`addiu a0,sp,60; lw a0,0(a0)`). That is a by-value `igResult` return used in place. Declaring the callee with an output pointer and passing `&local.v` gives named locals, which take the top slots in declaration order ahead of every temporary, and a test reads the slot directly. The RPC connection's `Bind`, `Call` and `CallWithData` and `igPsx2_LoadIopModule(Ex)` return `igResult`; their bodies end in `return g_resultFailure;` and `return *result;`, which compile as the stores through the hidden pointer did.

title: An argument cast to `int` for a variadic callee lets a loop hoist it.
symptom: In a loop calling `igStringObj_Format(path, "%s/%s", ...)`, retail rebuilds the format's address before every call; passed as `(int)DAT_004f9a78` to a callee declared `(int, int, ...)` the address moves into a saved register before the loop (one more `sq`, 12 bytes longer). With the callee declared `(igStringObj *, const char *, ...)` and the arguments passed as pointers, the address stays at the call.

title: A pointer argument cast to `int` takes a new allocator id.
symptom: `igStringObj_Trim` kept `self` in `s1` and the duplicated text in `s0`; with `igObject_DuplicateString(int self, int string)` called as `((int)self, ...)` the two swapped, whatever the declaration order or loop spelling. Declared `char *(void *self, const char *string)` and called with `self` itself, retail's registers follow.

title: A member release with a null test of the member's address is an explicit destructor call.
symptom: A class's hand-written destructor releases each reference field behind `addiu v0,s1,68; beqz v0; lw a0,68(s1)`. It is `((igSmartPointer<igObject> *)&p->_field)->~igSmartPointer();` (and `~igStringRef()` for a string field): the expanded destructor keeps its test of `this`. A helper spelling the test (`T **self = &field; if (self)`) is not the source.

title: A list's inserted pointer word is a class member.
symptom: `sw v0,104(sp); lw v1,104(sp); beqz v1` before the reference increment and `List_InsertWords(list, index, 1, &word)`: the word is the member of a one-word class with a retaining constructor (`RetainedWord<T>`), read back after the constructor's store. A pointer local or parameter whose address is passed is tested from the register and stored in the branch's delay slot (712 bytes against 716). A word built inside an inline helper is allocated after the caller's earlier inline parameters; where retail has it first, the word is declared in the function.

title: A class result read through a member function is read through its address.
symptom: After the `jalr`, `addiu v1,sp,332` and later `lw v1,0(v1)`: `tracker->vfunc_27(offset, &record).get()` on an `igResult` returned by value. Reading the member (`.v`) loads the slot directly (460 bytes against 464), and an `int` return has no result slot (452). A second result struct with its own accessor is not needed.

title: An interned-string holder interns in its constructor.
symptom: A null test of the characters, the string pool created on first use, the intern call and a store to a stack slot, later released, is `igStringRef name(chars);`. The same sequence without the null test, followed by the release of the old token, is the assignment `name = chars;`. Holders with an adopting constructor fed by hand-written intern code were the same class.

title: String literals are read-only, and a `strcpy` from one is a fixed-size copy.
symptom: a two-byte string (`"\n"`) is copied with `lui; addiu; lh 0(v0); sh 0(v1)` from `.rodata`, and a `strcat` in the same function points at the same object. Under the unit's flags a two-byte literal is small data (`-sdatathreshold 2` counts size 2), reached through `gp`, and `strcpy` stays a call; a `static const` array is copied byte by byte.
cause: the original build made string constants read-only (`-str readonly`). A read-only literal goes to `.rodata` whatever its size, and because its bytes cannot change the compiler expands `strcpy(buffer, "\n")` into a copy of the literal's known size; the variadic `int strcpy(...)` declaration is expanded the same way. Every two-byte string of the library sits in `.rodata` in retail, which is why the unit could only name them through extern arrays.
spelling: the literals written in the function, between `#pragma push`, `#pragma readonly_strings on` and `#pragma pop`: the pragma is the source form of the flag and leaves the unit's row alone. Each literal the function then emits is an `anon` row at its retail address. Equal literals are one object across the functions written this way: a later function's `"%s"` is the first one's, so the retail addresses a function reads show which earlier function's literals it shares.

title: A size parameter's conversion leaves the loop's entry jump at the end of the function.
symptom: the code before a `while` loop jumps to a two-instruction block placed after the function's last statement, which jumps on to the loop's test (`b L; ... L: b test+4; <copy of the test's first instruction>`), and the final `return` branches over that block: 12 bytes more than the same loop entered directly.
cause: the loop body passes an `int` to a callee whose parameter is unsigned (`strncat`'s `size_t`). The conversion is a loop-invariant expression, so the optimizer creates a preheader for the loop, and it appends new blocks at the end of the function. The moved value is a copy of the variable's register and vanishes in the code generator; the block stays. An empty preheader (nothing moved) is removed by jump chaining, so a callee declared with an `int` size has no such block.
spelling: the callee's real prototype, `char *strncat(char *, const char *, unsigned int)`, the argument passed plain.

title: A predicate that returns a byte is normalised before the branch.
symptom: `and v0,v0,v1; sltu v0,zero,v0; beqz v0` on a flag test: the test is an inline returning `unsigned char` whose body compares (`return (flags & mask) != 0;`). A `bool` return, or the mask test written in the `if`, folds to the plain branch. The object goes in by `const` reference: a pointer to `const` makes the field's address a value of its own (`addiu v0,s4,20`).

title: A range test spelled as an unsigned difference keeps it.
symptom: `addiu t4,c,-99; sltiu at,t4,5; bnez at` inside a chain of `beq` tests is `(unsigned)(c - 'c') > 4` (with `<=` for the other sense). `c >= 'c' && c <= 'g'` gives two `slti` tests, a run of `c != 'c' && c != 'd' && ...` gives one `beq` each and is not merged, and a `switch` sorts its cases, so a chain in retail's own unsorted order (`u x i s S c-g C ] n-p`) is a flat `&&` chain. The spelling was found by a variant test.

title: A large buffer that receives a literal's own size is a `strcpy` under read-only strings.
symptom: A 256-byte frame slot filled by a 15-byte copy (`ld`, `lwc1`/`swc1`, `lh`, `lbu` from the literal) and then passed to `strcat` is `char name[256]; strcpy(name, "igMetaObject: ");` with the literal read-only (the readonly-strings entry above). `char name[] = "igMetaObject: ";` copies the same 15 bytes into a 15-byte slot (the frame 256 bytes short), a larger array with the initialiser copies a template of the array's full size (`lq` loop), `memcpy` stays a call, and an array declared and never used takes no frame space.

title: A bit test returning `int` from `!= 0` is materialised before the branch.
symptom: Retail's `andi; sltu; bnez` comes from `static inline int hasValidity(...) { return (meta._validity & bit) != 0; }` tested as `if (!hasValidity(...))`; the same helper returning `bool` folds into `andi; bnez`, and `== true` compares with `1` (`bne v0,v1`).

title: `sltu; xori; xori; andi 0xff` is an `int`-to-`bool` conversion compiled with the peephole pass off.
symptom: two functions (0x32ef20, 0x32f060) turn bit 0 of the COP0 status into a `bool` with that sequence; no other function in the executable has two `xori 1` on one register. The same two functions copy their receiver to a saved register and read `_semaID` through that copy (`move s1,a1` … `lw a0,12(s1)`) where every other function keeps reading through the incoming `a1`.
cause: the code generator writes a conversion to `bool` as `x != 0` and two logical nots (`sne; xori 1; xori 1`, fresh temporaries each), and a store into a `bool` as `andi 0xff`. The block peephole pass then removes them. Its `xori` handler (0x512df0) turns the second `xori` into a copy of the first one's source when the value it reads was produced in the same block by an `xori` with the same immediate, that source is not written again in between (0x4bdf10), and the first `xori` does not write its own source (0x511f20); the first then dies, and the `andi 0xff` of a value known to be 0 or 1 becomes a copy as well. The same pass propagates copies (0x512050), which is what replaces a copied parameter by its argument register. Two things skip the pass, and all three effects then appear together (both `xori`, the `andi 0xff`, and the unpropagated copy of the receiver): an `__asm__ volatile(...)` statement, for the block that holds it (a plain `__asm__`, an `asm { }` block and an `asm` function do not stop the pass), and `#pragma peephole off` in force at the function's definition (it has to cover the function the conversion is expanded into; around an inline helper alone it does nothing).
spelling:
the read as one `__asm__ volatile("mfc0 $5, $12
	srl $6, $5, 16
	and $5, $5, $6
	move %0, $5" : "=r"(status))` in an inline helper, and `bool interruptsEnabled = interruptEnableStatus() & 1;` in the function. Without the keyword the conversion folds to one `sltu`.
notes: What does not give it: Plain C under the unit's profile: each `!` on a variable starts with its own `sltu`, a nested `!!` is one tree of fresh temporaries, and the pass folds it (some 60,000 generated spellings over three attempts). An `asm` function: b52 never expands one (`static inline asm`, `inline asm`, `asm inline`, `#pragma always_inline on`, with or without the `jr ra`); the caller gets a `jal`. The instructions written in an `asm { }` block on a local: a pair in one block survives (the first writes its own source), but an `asm` instruction that names a hard register is a barrier for the scheduler, `sltu x,zero,x` names `zero`, and the `lw a0,12(s1)` of the next statement then comes after the `sltu` where retail has it after the `and`. Retail's order is that of a three-instruction block followed by compiled code. *The status read names `a1`:* with the read's register left to the compiler (the `"=r"` operand of the statement in `src/engine/dmaChannel.c`, or an `asm { }` block on a local) it is `v1`, with the mask in `a1`; retail has both in `a1`. `mfc0 $5, $12; srl $6, $5, 16; and $5, $5, $6; move %0, $5` gives it, and the `move` is coalesced away. The statement needs no clobber list. *The receiver's two registers:* with the pass off a `const` copy of the parameter keeps its own register: `const igPsx2Semaphore *semaphore = self;` declared first, the first read through `self` (`lw s0,12(a1)`) and the later ones through the copy.

The equivalent spelling: the three instructions in an `asm { }` block (`mfc0 a1,$12; srl a2,a1,16; and a1,a1,a2; move status,a1`) with the function inside `#pragma push` / `#pragma peephole off` / `#pragma pop` gives the same bytes for both functions, and retail does not say which the original had. With the pass off for whole functions, the two before the pair (0x32ede0, 0x32eea0) differ and the ones after it, up to 0x32f380, are the same either way.

title: A value an inline reads for itself is evaluated after its arguments.
symptom: two expansions of one header-writing inline in one function; the one in a block that starts with an extra `addu` has `li a3,-1` and `move a2,s0` exchanged, two masks issued in the other order and one temporary in another register (5 instructions), and no declaration order or spelling of the surrounding statements moves it.
cause: the candidate passed the pool index as an argument, so its load was written ahead of the copies of the other arguments (arguments are evaluated from the last to the first). The first scheduling pass issues in list order, two a cycle; with the load first and the extra `addu` at the head, the header byte's load fell one cycle later than the index's, its user became ready one cycle after the index's user instead of with it, and the two ended in the other order. The live ranges then overlapped and the allocator needed another register. With the index read inside the inline the copies come first and both blocks schedule as retail.
spelling: the inline takes the object and reads the member itself, as a member function would.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (the arena allocator, 0x318110; traced with the scheduler trace).

title: A shared sum is computed where it is first used.
symptom: a block starts with a load in retail (`lw a0,200(s4)`) and with an `addu` in the candidate, and the branches into the block carry a copy of that `addu` in their delay slots where retail has `nop`.
cause: the candidate assigned `newTop = oldTop + nb` and then used `newTop` in the next expression, so the `addu` and the store of the spilled `newTop` were written first. The store ahead of the load makes the load wait for it in the second pass, the sum's chain is then the longest, and the `addu` leads the block. Retail has the load first, so the sum was written inside the expression that uses it.
spelling: `newEnd = (oldTop + nb + minimum + pageMask) & ~pageMask; newTop = oldTop + nb;`: the optimizer shares the sum, and its temporary is assigned where the first statement evaluates it. An assignment inside the expression gives the same bytes and is not needed.

title: Statement order shows in a delay slot.
symptom: `beqz at,L; nop; lw a0,56(s4); li v1,1; subu v0,v0,a0; sw v1,196(s4)`: the size is computed first and the state flag stored after it. With the store first its `li` fills the branch's slot and the load follows.

title: An argument of integer type is evaluated ahead of the format string.
symptom: `lui a0; lui v0; addiu a1,s3,8; addiu a0,a0,lo` in retail and the two `addiu`s exchanged in the candidate, in two of three sibling reports; the third, whose address is `block + oldHeadBytes`, matches.
cause: with the address passed as a pointer sum the argument registers are loaded in order, the format string first. Cast to an integer the sum is computed before the arguments are loaded, and the second scheduling pass, which falls back on list order between equal instructions, keeps it ahead.
spelling: `igReportNotice(format, (unsigned)block + 8u, 0xBBBBBBBF, *tail)`: the format prints the address with `%x`.

title: EE GCC orders stores only within one alias set; a field's or read's type decides the schedule.
symptom: Two memory accesses are kept in order when they may alias, and the alias set comes from the lvalue's type. Before register allocation only same-type accesses through the same base are ordered; after it the base registers are set more than once, so every pair in one alias set is ordered, and an access of another type (a pointer read among integer stores) is outside that chain, gets low priority and is issued ahead of the first store. Giving a field the same pointer type as another, or reading a reply through its true type, changes the order of the instructions around it.

title: In a run of independent stores, the one that ends a register's life is issued first.
symptom: Before register allocation the scheduler breaks a tie between equally ready instructions in favour of the one that frees registers. Stores of one value through one pointer all become ready together, so the last statement, which holds the last use of the pointer and of the value, comes out first and the others follow in source order; a store that ends only one register's life (the second of two 64-bit fields among 32-bit ones, which has the last use of the 64-bit constant) comes right after it. Retail's `+28, +0, +4, ... +24` is therefore a struct reset written in field order, and a source transcribed in retail's order is rotated once more. MWCC emits stores in source order, so such a transcription matches under MWCC and reads as a function built by the other compiler. The `.sched` dump shows it: every store has the same priority and the one carrying the `REG_DEAD` notes heads the ready list.

title: What the filler takes.
symptom: Read from the compiler (0x4c7690) and checked with the block dump. For a branch whose slot the instruction above cannot fill it tries, in order: the first instruction of the target, moved when the target has one predecessor and copied otherwise (an unconditional jump always may; a conditional branch only when the instruction's destination is in neither the live-in nor the live-out set of the block that ends with the branch); then the first instruction of the fall-through block, on the same liveness test and only when that block has **exactly one** predecessor. Loads, stores and calls are never taken. `v0` is live at the exit of every function that does not return a class, `void` ones included, so it is live from entry to the first call of a `void` function; a parameter still in its argument register is live-in to the entry block, so an instruction that reuses that register is not taken there.

title: Slots left empty across a whole function: the predecessor lists were emptied.
symptom: instructions and registers match, and three branches near the end of the function have a `nop` where the candidate fills the slot with the first instruction of the `if` body (12 bytes short). Nested `if`s and inline helpers change nothing.
cause: the block pass that runs before the filler retargets a conditional branch whose target begins with an unconditional jump, deletes a jump to the next block and merges a block into its only predecessor. After any one of these it sets every block's predecessor list to empty and does not rebuild it. With no predecessors recorded the filler takes nothing from a fall-through block anywhere in the function; copies from targets still happen. The optimizer removes such jumps itself, so one reaches the block pass only when it appears in the code generator: a `return` that is not the function's last statement, or a block whose only statement is a copy the register allocator coalesces away.
spelling: the walk of the free list is a `for` loop that reads the head again in its first clause, `else { for (next = self->freeHead; next < end; next += link * 4) { ... } }`, after `next = self->freeHead` was tested in the `if`. The second read is shared with the first, the copy into `next` is coalesced, and the `else` block is left holding only the jump to the loop's test, which the block pass retargets. With `for (; next < end; ...)` the three slots are filled. A `return;` closing the last `if` body gives retail's bytes too (the jump to the epilogue is deleted) and has no reason.

title: A register whose last use fills a delay slot stays live for the filler until the next barrier.
symptom: A loop's closing branch carries the loop-head compare in its slot and leaves a `move a0,…` behind it, where another spelling of the same statements puts that move in the slot and pads the loop head. The filler asks what is live on a branch's other path before it takes an instruction that sets a register, and at a label with no barrier before it the answer is a scan from the start of the function in which a register dies only at a `REG_DEAD` note (`mark_target_live_regs`). An instruction moved into a slot loses those notes (`emit_delay_sequence`). So when a register's last use is the instruction that fills an earlier branch's slot, the register counts as live at every later label, an instruction that sets it cannot leave a branch's fall-through (MIPS has no annul-if-true slot), and the filler copies from the branch target instead, whatever the branch's predicted direction. Which register that is follows from the locals: in the unit below, three fields of one global read into three locals in field order put the global's address in `a0` and the second field in `v1`, and testing the second field straight from the global swaps the two. The compiler binary keeps its symbols, so gdb breakpoints on `fill_slots_from_thread`, `mostly_true_jump`, `own_thread_p` and `mark_target_live_regs` print each decision and the live set behind it.

title: A deleted jump to the next block stops fall-through filling for the whole function.
symptom: most conditional branches keep a `nop` where another spelling fills the slot from the following instruction (`beq v0,a0,L; nop; li v1,2` where siblings have `beq v0,a0,L; li v1,2`). Copies from a branch target still fill slots, and the copied original stays in place as dead code (`bnez s4,L+4; slti at,…` with the same `slti` still at `L`). Every slot in the function changes together, whether the cause comes before or after it in the source. Small test files reproduce it.
cause: when the code generator deletes an unconditional jump whose target is the next block, the scheduler stops filling slots from the fall-through for the whole function. The front end has already removed its own redundant jumps, so only jumps made later count. Three constructs produce one: a `return;` closing the last `if` block of a function that returns `void`, or `igResult`, which comes back through a hidden pointer (`if (bad) { report(); return; }` as the final statement); a conditional expression whose condition ends in a logical not as the last operand of `&&` or `||` (`f(x == -1 && !p ? a : b)`; the same condition in an `if` does not count, and neither does `p == 0`); a `switch` with `default:` written before its cases.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp`: the arena pool's block walks (0x311d10, a trailing `return;` after the bad-chunk report) and the arena block check (0x312790, `igResult`).
notes: Reading it: when retail has the `nop` slots, look for which of these the function used. One that also changes the branch it sits in (`!p` turns `beqz p,T; b F` into `bnez p,F`) is the wrong one. An `int` or pointer return has no `return;` form; there the trigger has to be one of the other two.

title: A copy the allocator coalesces away leaves a jump the block pass retargets.
symptom: a function has the unfilled slots of the entry above and none of its three constructs; its instructions match with every obvious spelling and only the slots differ (15 `nop`s in a 324-instruction function).
cause: the block pass has three rules, read from the compiler (0x4c6b80) and reported per block by the block dump: it retargets a conditional branch whose target block begins with an unconditional jump, it deletes a jump to the next block, and it merges a block that ends with a jump or the return into its only predecessor when that predecessor falls into it. Any of them empties the predecessor lists. The first one fires when the last statement of an `if` body is a copy between two variables that the register allocator gives one register: `if (pages != 0) { …; if (self->updateStatistics) { …call… } result = pages; } else { …; result = 0; }`. The copy's block is then only the jump over the `else`, and the `updateStatistics` test branches to it. Assigning `result` straight from the calls gives the same instructions with filled slots.
notes: Evidence for the source: the GameCube build of the same function keeps the two variables apart (`mr r29,r25` in front of the jump over the failure arm), and its allocator calls all write `r25`.

Reading it: when a function is in this mode and no jump-making construct fits, run the block dump on the candidate with a suspect spelling and look for the changed block; in the other builds look for a register copy that the PS2 build does not have.

title: A commutative add takes the plain variable as its first operand.
symptom: The front end orders the operands of `+` so that a leaf comes first. An inline call counts as complex until it is expanded, and a conditional expression is always complex. To get retail's `addu v1,a0,v1` with the payload in `a0`, the payload has to be a variable. When the value is only computed after the guards of a check, that means splitting the `&&` chain into nested `if`s and assigning the variable between them: `if (level > 0 && ml > 0) { size = …; if (((Chunk *)((char *)h + (size + header)))->used && ml > 0) … }` compiles to the same branches as the flat chain.

title: A statement after an `if` that both arms reach is hoisted into the test's slot.
symptom: after a scan loop, `bnez t7,L; li s0,2` with the append in the fall-through, and the loop's first exit to that test keeps a `nop`. With the assignment written ahead of the `if` the `li` stays in front of the branch, the slot takes the fall-through's first instruction, and the loop exit copies the `li` from its target. *Cause (not traced):* written after the `if`, the assignment is the first instruction of the join both paths reach, and it ends up in the test's slot; the test is then the first instruction at the loop exits' target, which leaves them nothing to copy. Written ahead, it stays in the test's own block and the slot takes the fall-through's first instruction. The two placements also number the temporaries differently.
spelling: `if (!space) { piece[used++] = c; i++; } state = 2;`.

title: Declaration order, getters and helper argument order decide ids.
symptom: A count declared before a cast list pointer (`int count; List *list = (List *)target; count = list->_count;`) gives the list the lower saved register; the natural order swaps them.
unit_text: `src/game/beNDMWShopCtrl00.cpp`. A value an inline helper returns, and a helper's own locals, are numbered with the inline's values; using the getter (`work = buildData(self)`) and the setter inline together gives retail's order where hand-ordered locals stood before. / `src/game/beDemoManager.cpp`. An inline's arguments are evaluated before its body: `AppendRecordString(self->_messenger, db, record, key)` loads the messenger into a saved register before the call inside it. / `src/game/beNDMWShopCtrl00.cpp`.

title: A class local is numbered after every declared local, wherever it is declared.
symptom: instructions identical, two saved registers exchanged between a result object and a pointer local (`s2`/`s3`). The result declared `int` and read as `.v` matches; declared as its class it does not, and no declaration position of it or of the other locals changes anything.
cause: a class local is not a register candidate. `IRO_ScalarizeClassDataMembers`, the first phase of the optimizer's loop, replaces its one member with a temporary (`*(result) = ...` becomes `*(@1793) = ...` in the dump), and the temporary takes its allocator id then: after all the function's declared locals, mid-block ones included, and after the parameters of the inlines already expanded (`operator==`'s `this`), but before the optimizer's later temporaries and before the second and later webs of a reused variable. Retail colours the pointer first, so the pointer has the later id. No declared pointer can have one; a later web of a variable the function reuses does. Traced: block-local pointer 42, result 49, result coloured first; pointer as a later web 62, result 48, retail's colours.
spelling: `igResult result = g_resultSuccess;`, and the new pool kept in the function's one pool pointer, which the loops before and after it also use, not in a block-local of its own. With the pointer reused both `int` and `igResult` match, so the `int` only compensated for the block-local.

title: An argument that carries an integer conversion is loaded before the plain ones.
symptom: a call passes two fields of one row as its third and fourth arguments and loads the fourth first, with the row pointer in the third's register (`lw a3,4(a2); lw a2,0(a2)`); the plain spelling loads them in order with the row in `a3`. A `(long long)` cast on the fourth argument gives retail's order although the parameter is 32-bit.
cause: the two spellings differ in the IR by one conversion node on that argument. Any conversion to an integer type does it: an implicit one between `int` and `unsigned`, a byte field widened to an `int` or `unsigned` parameter, `(int)` written on an `int` or on a pointer. A cast to a pointer type does not (it is a node too, but it does not count). Of the four combinations (conversion on the third, the fourth, both, neither) the fourth is loaded first exactly when it carries one, and the row pointer takes the register of the argument loaded last. Where the base pointer is not in an argument register, two arguments that both carry a conversion, or neither, are loaded in order.
spelling: the field and the parameter in their own types, which differ in sign: `unsigned size` in the row, `int size` in the callee, the argument passed plain. An `int` field with an `unsigned` parameter gives the same bytes, here and in the callee's other callers; the row's size is printed as `0x%08x` beside its addresses, so the field is the unsigned one.
notes: The reverse case: retail loads a list handle before the byte flag passed after it (`lw a3,192(s1); lbu t0,168(s1)`), and with the flag parameter declared `unsigned int` the flag is loaded first, because the widening is a conversion; `(List *)(int)file->_list` then repairs the order by giving the list one too. The parameter has the field's type, `unsigned char endianSwap`, so neither argument carries a conversion. In the callees the flag is tested plain, `if (endianSwap)`: `endianSwap != 0` promotes the byte, and the promotion the tests share becomes an `andi` into a register of its own (4 bytes more).

title: An `int` copy of a parameter at the top of a function stands for something else.
symptom: *A reassigned variable.* `m = m->_writeProxy ? proxy() : m` makes a second web of `m`, numbered after every declared local, so it colours before the count declared after it and takes its register (`s3`/`s4` exchanged; traced: list 35, `m` 37, count 39, second web of `m` 42). Copies of the list and flag parameters into `int` locals moved their ids instead. The source has two variables, each declared where it is first set: `meta`, `index`, `writeMeta`, `count`, `i`; of the declaration orders only those with `index` before `writeMeta` before `count` before `i` match. *A cast at a call inside a loop.* `(int)file` on a pointer parameter passed to a callee declared with an `int` is a loop-invariant expression: `IRO_MoveInvariantExpressions` computes it into a temporary before the loop, and when that value is spilled the frame has one more 4-byte slot (192 bytes against 176). The callee takes the pointer type and the parameter is passed plain.

title: A loop index started from a named value is declared last.
symptom: a walk over a list from a start count to an end count has the index and the end count in each other's saved register (`s0`/`s1`); the start count is loaded before the end count, so declaring the index first and assigning it there gives the wrong registers, and only an index declared after the count but assigned before it matched.
cause: the source names the start: `int first = base->_count; int count = fields->_count; for (int i = first; i < count; i++)`. The copy `i = first` is propagated, `first` never reaches the allocator and takes no id, and `i`, declared in the `for`, is numbered after `count` (traced: list 33, count 34, index 35; with `int i = base->_count; int count = ...` index 34, count 35).
spelling: as above, each local declared where it is first set. Four field walks of one class take this shape.

title: A value read through an inline getter is numbered after the declared locals.
symptom: a function loads three fields of one global into saved registers and then makes a call; the registers fit no declaration order in which the locals are declared where they are assigned. A search found an order with the first and third of them declared after locals that are first set much later.
cause: a local initialised from an inline function's return value takes the return temporary's id, which is made after all of the caller's declared locals (traced: the two values leave the declared range 33-47 and become node 71 and a neighbour). Controls: both getters are needed; either one alone, or neither, differs; the second field read plainly or through a getter makes no difference.
spelling: the two values through inline member getters of the object that holds them, the other field read directly, and every local declared at its first assignment, loop indices and block-locals in their blocks. No declaration order is left to choose.

title: A typed view of a `void *` parameter is copied where it is declared.
symptom: `beqz system,end; nop; lbu mode; bnez mode; move s1,a0`: the parameter's copy to a saved register sits in the second branch's delay slot and the first slot is empty. Declared at the top of the function the copy fills the first slot.
cause: the copy is an assignment and is emitted in the block that holds it; the delay-slot filler then moves it over the load into the next branch's slot.
spelling: the view declared as the first statement inside the `if (system)` block, the other locals after it where they are first set. A separate local for the mode byte is not needed.

title: C-style declarations at the top keep their order; parameters need no copies.
symptom: A duplicate search over a record table (`i`, `j`, a found flag, the value) has the value in `s0` and the flag in `s1`, though the value is set first: the four are declared together at the top as `int i, j, found; T *value;` (traced ids 34-37). The value or the flag declared in its block exchanges two registers. Six sibling functions share the order. Copies of the output pointer and the remaining count into locals changed nothing: the parameters are stepped directly. The same class walks its records with a pointer declared before the index (`record++` beside `i++`) where retail keeps a stepped pointer, and indexes `records[i]` where retail multiplies on every pass; the unit builds for size and does not turn one into the other.

title: A pointer an inline getter returns is numbered after the caller's block locals.
symptom: a configure function reads strings from its info record at the top and parses each in a block with a local of its own (a flags word, a level); retail gives the block local the higher saved register, the plain spelling gives it to the string, and the only declaration order that matches has the block locals declared at the top, ahead of the strings.
cause: the string read through an inline getter that returns the pointer is the getter's result, numbered with the inline's values after every local the caller declares, block locals included, so it colours first. The getter's parameter may be `const` or not. An `int` getter with the cast at the call, an `int` local and a plain field read all keep the declared local's early number.
spelling: `const char *messages = igMemoryPoolInfo_messages(info);` with `static inline const char *igMemoryPoolInfo_messages(const igMemoryPoolInfo *info)`, every local declared where it is first set, the result an `igResult` assigned from the base call.

title: A decoder's helpers take the cursor and the result by reference, and the results are typed scratch locals.
symptom: a record decoder runs a variable-length-integer loop per field. Retail keeps the read pointer in one saved register throughout, the flags word in the next and the slot counter between them; the value and the shift of a field's loop sit in `a1` and `a0`. Helpers that return the advanced pointer, or that build the value in a local of their own and store it at the end, give the same instructions with the saved registers rotated and the value and shift exchanged; no declaration order of the caller's locals changes anything, because each is replaced by a helper's temporary.
cause: a helper that works on `T &out` directly (`out = 0; out |= ...`) leaves the caller's declared variable as the accumulator, with the id of its declaration; the helper's own locals (shift, a copy of the cursor) are numbered after it. Only the first web of a declared variable has that id: a scratch variable used for a second field is a later web and is numbered after the helper's locals, which exchanges the two registers. Retail's pattern (declared-variable order at the type, at the first signed field and at the first unsigned field after it, later-web order everywhere else) is three variables: the type, one signed scratch and one unsigned scratch, each field assigned from the scratch of its own signedness.
spelling: `static inline void decodeUnsigned(const char *&p, unsigned int &out)` and `decodeSigned(const char *&p, int &out)`, called as `decodeSigned(p, value); record->size = value;`.
notes: The cursor copy: each helper reads through a local copy (`const char *q = p; ... p = q;`). The copy's last assignment back is then an expression the optimizer puts into the next use in the same block, so where two fields are decoded with a call between them and no branch, the cursor's increment comes after the call's result is stored (`jal; lw a0,68(s4); sw v0,68(s3); addiu s0,s0,1`), not in the call's delay slot.

title: A character compared in place needs no local.
symptom: A scan `while (*s && *s != '\'' && n < 255)` whose body tests and stores `*s` again shares one load and one sign extension; copying the character to an `int` local in the condition (`(c = *s) != '\''`) gives the same instructions with eight temporaries permuted.

title: Stack slots rise as allocator ids fall, and a split lifetime has a late id.
symptom: instructions and registers match and two or three spilled values sit in each other's 16-byte slots (`sw zero,208(sp)` against `sw zero,256(sp)`), or the entry block zeroes two slots in the other order.
cause: the slots are handed out upwards from the highest id to the lowest. Ids are: declared locals in declaration order, then the optimizer's temporaries in the order it makes them (a shared mask or a shared `unsigned short` to `int` conversion among them), then the temporaries of `IRO_SplitLifetimes`. That phase gives a variable with several separate lifetimes (zeroed at entry and set again on the reallocation path, and set and used on its own on the free path) a new temporary for every lifetime but the second it finds in statement order; so the lifetime that starts at the entry assignment has a late id, and the one on the free path keeps the declared one. It handles the variables in the order the function first refers to them, a dead initialiser included, and makes one variable's temporaries together. The scheduler trace prints the ids (`D:c0r90 U:c0r0` is `r90 = 0`), and the optimizer dump after `IRO_SplitLifetimes` shows the temporaries by name.
spelling: declarations in the order the slots of the unsplit variables fall (`int newBytes; int total; bool moved; int oldHeadBytes;` for slots 256, 240, 224, 208), and the entry assignments as statements in the order of the stores.
