One function needs `int oldHeadBytes = 0;` ahead of `oldSize = 0; oldBytes = 0; oldHeadBytes = 0;`: the dead initialiser only makes it the first of the three the phase handles. What the original's earlier reference was is not known. The GameCube build zeroes exactly the split variables with register copies (`li r26,0; mr r19,r26; mr r24,r26`) and the others with `li`, which shows which variables the original reused across the free and reallocation paths.
notes: Open: the malloc pool's sibling (0x3236a0) shows the same three copies on GameCube, yet matches on PS2 only with the free path's sentinel offset in a local of its own: with the variable reused there its entry lifetime takes a late id and its slot falls below the shared alignment's. One source for both functions has not been found.

title: Spilled locals take their stack slots from the last declared to the first.
symptom: A function with more long-lived locals than saved registers keeps some in 16-byte frame slots; the slots rise in the reverse of declaration order, so their offsets give the declaration block. Where a value returned after a scoped block has a slot below the block's own locals, the locals are all declared at the top of the function, C style, and only the scoped object is in the block. The hidden result pointer of a function that returns a class is kept differently when registers run out: it goes to a 4-byte slot beside the address-taken locals (`sw a0,360(sp)` at entry, loaded at each `return`), not to a 16-byte slot.

title: Fields read where they are used leave no locals to order.
symptom: A reader's `gets` compares, clamps and subtracts its position and length: `if (f->pos >= f->len) return 0;` and `if (n + f->pos >= f->len) n = f->len - f->pos;`. The shared reads are the optimizer's temporaries, numbered as it makes them; `int len = f->len; int pos = f->pos;` loads the same two words into exchanged registers, and matched only with the locals declared in the reverse of the order they are set.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2ecea0, 0x32bdd0). A stack pool's free space is `(unsigned)(pool->end + 1) - pool->top` straight from the fields, and the running `end` and `low` are declared in the branch that walks them; the padding step reads `pool->top` in place (`mask & (align - (pool->top & mask))`, `out[i] = pool->top + pad`). Locals for the top, declared at the head of the function, exchanged registers and changed the order of the size arithmetic. **A reused index is numbered late.** One `unsigned i` serving every loop of a function has a web per loop, and each web after the first is numbered after all the declared locals, so the index takes a lower register than the locals of the loop it runs. An index per loop takes the higher one. Seventeen locals whose order a search had found reduce to the function written this way, with the count an `unsigned short` parameter used directly (its widened copy is the compiler's and takes the lowest register, where a declared count local took a higher one). / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x327d40, 0x327ed0). A scanf over a format string reads `format[i]` at each use in the outer dispatch (`if (format[i] != '%')`, `piece[used++] = format[i]`), and only the inner conversion scan keeps the character in a local, `c`, with the space test through a one-line inline (`static inline int isSpace(int c) { return _ctype_[c + 1] & 8; }`). A character local for the outer dispatch, declared anywhere, exchanged it with the hoisted copy of the format pointer (`t1`/`t2`); without the inline, ten temporaries took other registers. / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2ec980, 0x32b8d0).

title: Where a pair of locals is all that is left of an order.
symptom: `for (int i = 0, count = list->count; i < count; i++)` numbers the index before the count, which a count declared in front of the loop does not; an `int` getter for the count changes nothing.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2e8c40). Two values that never cross a call share the argument registers, and the later-numbered takes `a0`: a heap walk's next-block pointer is declared with the function's other pointers, ahead of its `ok` flag, and every other local sits where it is first set. / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x312790). An index declared at the head of the function (`int i; int seen = 0; bool found = false;`) is numbered before the counters zeroed beside it and takes the higher temporary register. / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x306510).

title: The front end orders the operands of a commutative operator.
symptom: `addu v1,v1,a0` where retail has `addu v1,a0,v1`, and exchanging the operands in the source changes nothing.
cause: MWCC rewrites `a + b` before the optimizer runs; the first phase of the IR dump already shows the new order. A plain variable goes ahead of an expression, and the shorter of two expressions first. A call of an inline function is an expression at that point, even one that expands to a single temporary, so `size(p) + (p->words + 1) * 4` becomes `(p->words + 1) * 4 + @temp`.
spelling: give the term retail adds first a local of its own (`payload = size(p); total = payload + ...`), or put the whole sum in the inline, where the left term is the inline's own local.

title: An inline's return value replaces the variable it is assigned to.
symptom: two saved registers exchanged, and no declaration order of the locals moves them.
cause: in `total = sum(p)` copy propagation replaces `total` with the inline's return temporary, which takes its allocator id after every declared local. A local assigned an expression that only contains the inline's result (`total = payload + ...`) keeps the id of its declaration.
spelling: as above; the destination then colours by where it is declared.

title: A value read through an accessor inline is numbered with the inline's values.
symptom: A saved flag (`used = usedBit(p)`), a link store whose value is loaded (`setForward(p, *bin)`) and a size kept in a named local rather than updated in place each gave retail's temporaries where the written-out expression exchanged two of them.

title: m2c offset variables steal saved registers.
symptom: A user `offset += 4` with `data + offset` is a source variable coloured before the slot pointer; an index loop over `&data[i]` lets the compiler make the offset itself, with retail's registers. Rewrite m2c's strength-reduced loops as index loops first.

title: A derived view of a base-class parameter keeps the argument register.
symptom: A traversal function that takes `igTraversal *traversal`, works through `igCompileTraversal *self = (igCompileTraversal *)traversal;` and passes `traversal` on to the next traversal function keeps the incoming `a0` live for that call: the code between avoids `a0` and the call has no `move a0,s0`. One pointer used for both gives the move and shifts every temporary.

title: Inline virtuals are emitted in reverse declaration order.
symptom: Declare them in the reverse of retail's address order.

title: A later web of a reused variable colours first; a block local is its own first web.
symptom: instructions identical, the temporaries of one path rotated (`v1`/`a0`, then every temporary after them), and no order of the declarations changes it.
cause: `IRO_SplitLifetimes` gives each separate lifetime of a variable after the first a new temporary, numbered late, so it colours before the optimizer's shared values and takes the low register. The value retail colours late is a variable's first lifetime. In the dlmalloc code one `bck` holds the chunk before the victim in the small-bin path, in the unsorted loop, in binning and in the bin scan; retail's colours need the first two to be lifetimes of their own.
spelling: the value declared in the block that uses it (`TaggedBlockHeader *previous = ...;` in the small-bin path and again in the unsorted loop), the function-level variable left to the paths that share it. The reverse case in the same allocator: the end and the new top of a separately placed system block are the function's `newEnd` and `newTop` assigned a second time, which is what gives them the first temporary registers; a local for the end exchanges three temporaries, and the sum written out at both uses is computed after the alignment test instead of before it.

title: A named local keeps an argument out of the inline's arithmetic.
symptom: `addiu a2,s5,-8; addiu a0,a2,-4; ... addiu v0,a2,-12`: the argument is computed once and the inline subtracts from it. Passed as an expression (`resize(chunk, size - 8)`) the constants fold (`-12`, `-20` from the variable); a `const` parameter changes nothing, a cast on the argument stops the folding but numbers the value differently.
spelling: `unsigned int shortened = size - 8; resize(chunk, shortened);`.

title: Locals declared in the order they are first assigned.
symptom: A search over the declaration order of fourteen locals found one that matched; testing every single move showed only five constraints, and the order of first assignment satisfies them all. Try that order before searching.

title: A 64-bit member passed as `%u` is read through a getter.
symptom: a notice passes twelve 64-bit counters truncated to 32 bits. Retail loads the first five whole (`ld`) before the branch of a conditional argument and truncates them after it (`dsll32`/`dsra32`), loads the seven that go to the stack with `lw`, all of them ahead of the stores; the candidate loads and stores one by one and reads the first five with `lw` after the conditional.
cause: a cast on the member is narrowed to a 32-bit load in the optimizer and is then a plain operand, loaded where its argument register is set. An inline getter returning `long long` leaves a 64-bit temporary assigned where the call stands, so every argument is evaluated before any is placed, and the truncation happens at placement; within one block the load and the truncation merge into `lw`.
spelling: `(unsigned int)pool->getLocalAllocated()` with `long long getLocalAllocated()`.

title: An `int` accessor materialises a flag test.
symptom: `andi v0,v0,0x40; sltu v0,zero,v0; beqz v0`: the option test goes through an inline returning `int` (`return (flags & option) != 0;`). Written in place, or through an inline returning `bool`, the `sltu` is folded into the branch.

title: A copy that coalescing removes leaves its block behind.
symptom: `beqz at,L730` to a block that is only `b L1138`: the source assigns `newp = oldp` at the end of the first arm, both variables take one register, and the jump is not threaded because the block was not empty when jumps were chained. The statements after the arms use `newp`. An assertion written ahead of `remainder_size = newsize - nb` likewise leaves the subtraction on both sides of the notice.

title: A read through a `const` getter and a store to the member do not share the member's address.
symptom: a local record's member is read, then stored to inside a loop, each time straight off the stack (`lw v0,244(sp)` … `sw v0,244(sp)`); plain reads and stores put the member's address in a saved register for the whole block (`addiu s5,sp,292; lw v0,0(s5)` … `sw v0,0(s5)`) and the frame grows by the slots that displaces. In the same function a member read three times around calls does keep its address in a register (`addiu s5,sp,244; lw a0,0(s5)`).
cause: the address `&local + offset` is an expression `IRO_CommonSubs` shares when it is used twice on one path. A read through a `const` member function has its address node marked, the plain store's is not, so those two are different expressions; three plain reads are one.
spelling: `if (event.getSourceFile() == 0 || …) { int *frame = event.getCallStack(); … event.callStack = frame; event.f68 = path; }` with `const` getters on the record, and the later fields read plainly.

title: A by-value getter in a variadic call is read before a conditional argument.
symptom: `lb v0,976(sp); beqz v0,L; lw a2,184(sp)`: the value passed after `spec[0] != 0 ? spec : "0x%08x"` is loaded ahead of the conditional's branch. An inline getter's result is a temporary assigned where the call stands, before the conditional is evaluated; the member written in place is loaded where its argument register is set, after it. Pointer members tested first (`if (event.group != 0 && …)`) are already in a register and need no getter.

title: A pointer cast to `int` at several calls is one value in a saved register.
symptom: With the record's accessors declared `(int record, int slot)`, `(int)&event` at each call was shared as an expression and kept in `s5` from the top of the function, and every other saved register moved; declared with the record pointer, each call builds `addiu a0,sp,176` in place.

title: A `switch` with one case keeps the branch pair.
symptom: `beq v1,v0,body; nop; b past` for a block run for a single event type is `switch (event.type) { case 8: …; break; }`; `if (event.type == 8)` gives `bne v1,v0,past`. A `case 15:` written in front of `default:` shows in the jump table's bound (`sltiu at,v0,16`, not 15).

title: An element read through a reference accessor keeps `base + offset` when the index is hoisted.
symptom: `lw v1,16(v0); lw v0,176(sp); addu v0,v1,v0; lh v0,0(v0)`: the list's data plus a byte offset computed once in front of the loop. With `list->_data[index]` (or a by-value `get(index)`) the same two values are added the other way round, `addu v0,v0,v1`.
cause: `IRO_MoveInvariantsInAddressExpr` rewrites the address under an indirection inside a loop with the invariant part first, `(index << 1) + data`, before `IRO_MoveInvariantExpressions` moves the shift out. An accessor that returns a reference leaves the address in its return temporary through the first round of loop phases, so it is not under an indirection when that rewrite runs: only the shift is moved, the order stays as written, and the temporary is put back into the read in the next round.
spelling: `T &operator[](int index) { return _data[index]; }` on the list, `(*bases.p)[parentIndex]`.

title: Statement order decides which temporaries share a register with a reloaded spill.
symptom: `lw v0,208(sp); addiu s6,s6,1; lw v1,8(s4); addu s5,s5,v0; lhu v0,20(s4); addu v0,v1,v0`: the reloaded step and the size share `v0`, so the cursor's step was written ahead of the statement that reads the size (`slot++; field += step; meta->_sizeofSize = offset(field) + size(field);`). With the size update first, the reload overlaps both loads and takes a third register. The two members go through by-value getters: read in place, the widened `unsigned short` is evaluated ahead of the `int` on its left.

title: A `short` updated in place is sign-extended where it is computed.
symptom: `addu v0,s6,v0; dsll32 s6,v0,16; dsra32 s6,s6,16` ahead of a list append is `slot += bases[owner]; list->append(slot);` on a `short` local; the sum passed as the argument is truncated only by the store. The append is the list's own (`n = count(); if (n < _capacity) _count = _count + 1; else List_Resize(this, n + 1, sizeof(T));`): its count comes through the `const` accessor, so the increment reads the member again.

title: A local declared ahead of a spilled one colours after the scan that follows the spill.
symptom: a write position and the byte total it follows share `s5` where retail has `s0`, with the block pointer and the guard size one register low; no order of the function-level locals moves them.
cause: the allocator pushes low-degree nodes in ascending id, scan after scan, and colours in reverse. The last scan pushed the header pointers and the position first and the long-lived locals after them (`45 46 81 | 33 36 37 38`), so the position coloured after them. A position declared before the spilled `first` record pointer has a lower id than the header pointers, is pushed in the same scan as the long-lived locals and after them, colours first and takes `s0`; the byte total, which does not overlap it, then takes `s0` too.
spelling: in the block, `char *cursor; GangRecord *first; TaggedBlockHeader *h;`; at the top the guard before the block pointer.

title: A node one neighbour over the limit waits a scan and takes `v0`.
symptom: a size loop's index is in `v0` and every temporary one register up (`v1`, `a0`, …) where retail has the index in `a3`. The sibling function with one fewer spilled value matches with the same source.
cause: the index has 29 neighbours (traced with the proxy compiler); 25 or more keeps a node out of the scan until enough lower-numbered neighbours are pushed, and only four were (the loop's size, chunk and the inline's two values). Pushed in the second scan, it coloured before all the loop's temporaries. A fifth lower-numbered neighbour puts it in the first scan.
spelling: the member's size with its record is a variable set twice, `entry = chunk + 12; entry = roundUp8(entry); total += entry;`. A variable set once is propagated away and gives no node.

title: Mixed signedness keeps two additions, and two masks, apart.
symptom: `roundUp8(chunk + 12)` with an `int` parameter adds 12 and then 7 where two `unsigned` values fold to 19; a chunk size computed in `int` loads its own `-4` where an `unsigned` one reuses the mask already in a register. Each is a conversion node between the two operations.

title: A header written by the shared inline keeps the arithmetic its other callers need.
symptom: a function that always writes the 12-byte header computes the header word count at run time (`addiu a2,a1,12; subu a1,a2,a1; srl; addiu -1`), and with the statements written out the constant folds; with the fold prevented by a signed local the instructions are retail's but 79 sit elsewhere in the block, the `0 & 1` of the cleared flags in `t9` instead of `v0`.
cause: the pool's blocks are stamped by one inline that takes the block's byte count or 0 (`if (total == 0) total = ((size + 3) & ~3) + 12;` in the long branch, `+ 4` in the short one, then `words = ((total - ((size + 3) & ~3)) >> 2) - 1`) and a flag that forces the long form. The forced branch is removed after the subtraction has been built from two copies of the rounded size, so nothing folds, and the statements reach the scheduler in the inline's order.
spelling: `initBlockHeader(self, h, size, 0, marked, external)`; the two gang allocators and the system-block allocator share it.

title: A compare written toward the larger side branches through `at`.
symptom: `total + used <= max` gives retail's `sltu at,max,sum; bnez at` and puts the refused path out of line; `max >= sum` makes a register of the compare. `alignment > 8` likewise for `slti at,v0,9`.

title: A member call loads its argument before its object.
symptom: `lw a1,124(sp); jal; lw a0,64(s0)` where the candidate has `lw a0,64(s0); jal; lw a1,124(sp)`: the same two loads, the object's issued first. Casts, `get()` and an inline member wrapper change nothing. *Cause (not traced):* MWCC writes a member function's arguments before its `this`; the plain call wrote the object pointer first here. An inline wrapper is expanded and its call is plain again.
spelling: declare the out-of-line member on the class view (`int addDirectory(igObject *directory);`) and map its mangled name to the retail address in the unit's `externals`.

title: A virtual call's object read in its own statement is loaded ahead of a conditional argument.
symptom: Retail loads the object into `a1` in the slot of the branch that picks the text argument (`bnez a3,L; lw a1,148(sp)`); written in the call, the object is loaded at the join after the conditional expression. A local (`igInfoView *loader = (igInfoView *)poolInfo.p;`) before the call gives retail's order.

title: Discarded `igResult` temporaries take frame slots in the order they are made.
symptom: The first made has the highest slot. Calls written in an inline helper make their temporaries when the helper is expanded, after the caller's own, so two allocator loops moved into a helper gave their results the two lowest slots where retail has them above the one the function body makes later. Written in place, the loops give retail's slots. A named result local (`int copied; f(&copied, ...)`) takes a slot ahead of every temporary; the call returning `igResult` makes a temporary where it is.

title: An inline's parameter is numbered before its locals.
symptom: A string setter inline that takes the object as a parameter gives the interned token the first saved register and the object the second; retail has them the other way in one of two call sites. The tracer asks for the object's id after the token's; taking the holder by reference and reading the object into a local declared after the token gives it.

title: An `asm` statement without outputs is volatile already.
symptom: Its keyword does nothing; strip it. A review of the Sony kernel rows found 47 of their 63 keywords removable.

title: Sony's input-operand form.
symptom: A `$gp` store spelled with its word as an output (`"=m"`) can be moved and needs the keyword; Sony's text passes it as an input, `__asm__("sw $28,%0" : : "m"(word))`, which is fixed already. A `"memory"` clobber, as every helper in Sony's `eekernel.h` has, does what a keyword on a syscall statement did.

title: MWCC's `__I_<mnemonic>` builtins are inline assembly.
symptom: They emit one named instruction from C (`__I_mfc0(3, 12)`), and count as `asm` uses.

title: A `static` C function holding one `asm` block gives the same bytes and caller effect as an `asm` function.
symptom: The caller's argument registers stay live across a call to any `static` function defined earlier that contains inline assembly; that proves "static, earlier, contains asm", not "asm function".

title: Hand-written assembly shows in alignment and MMI.
symptom: A 4-aligned object or a loop top at 4 mod 8 under ee-gcc 2.96, `lui`/`ori` for -1 where 2.96 uses `addiu`, and MMI byte operations (`psubb`, `pcpyh`, `psubw`) with no C spelling: the R5900 string and memory routines.
